# gledach

> Free, installable tools that turn public data into information, insight and
> intelligence. Run them on your own machine. No account to start.

gledati (slav.): to watch. What a good analyst does before speaking.

gledach is a shelf, not a platform. The tools published here are written by the
same author but do not share a stack, an interface or a release cadence. What
they share is the promise below.

## House rules

- Free, and the source is public. MIT unless a dependency makes that impossible.
- Your machine is the runtime. Cloud is for sharing state between machines you own.
- No account to start. Keys, hosted databases and schedules are opt in, later.
- Honest about blind spots. Every tool ships a written audit of what it cannot see.
- Read only until you say otherwise. Paid actions ship disabled, behind a spend ceiling.
- Generated text is labelled as generated. Model output is not verified fact.

## The ladder

Every tool moves something public up four rungs and states where it stopped.

1. Data: what is already public. Feeds, filings, certificate logs, changed pages.
2. Information: collected, deduplicated, attributed.
3. Insight: scored and correlated.
4. Intelligence: queryable by something other than a person.

## Tools

### signal · rung 04, intelligence · live preview

Competitive intelligence your agents can query. Watches a market, turns public
noise into scored and attributed signals, exposes them over MCP. Ships tracking
thirteen AI coding agents and app builders; retargeted by editing one gitignored
file. Node, three runtime dependencies, no build step, libSQL storage that is a
local file by default.

- Repository: https://github.com/gledach/signals
- Live preview: https://signal.gledach.de (static export of a real deployment, dated, read only)
- Install guide: https://github.com/gledach/signals/blob/main/docs/start.md
- Agent surface (MCP): https://github.com/gledach/signals/blob/main/docs/mcp.md
- Blind spots: https://github.com/gledach/signals/blob/main/docs/blindspots.md
- Licence: MIT. Price: 0.

Install:

    git clone https://github.com/gledach/signals && cd signals
    npm install
    npm run db:migrate
    npm run view

Figures: 13 sources, 8 MCP tools (read only until a deployment opts in),
3 runtime dependencies, 2,600+ signals stored in the deployment behind the preview.

### signal-patterns · reference

How to build tools that watch the public web: what is watchable, what it costs,
how to build a watcher, and the engineering decisions that only become obvious
after something has broken. Nothing to install.

- Repository: https://github.com/gledach/signal-patterns
- What is watchable: https://github.com/gledach/signal-patterns/blob/main/sources.md
- What it costs: https://github.com/gledach/signal-patterns/blob/main/techniques.md
- Building a watcher: https://github.com/gledach/signal-patterns/blob/main/building-a-watcher.md
- Being consumable by agents: https://github.com/gledach/signal-patterns/blob/main/agent-integration.md

Thesis: the useful signals are the ones a company exposes before it means to.
Ordered by lead time: infrastructure (weeks), hiring (months, vague),
documentation (hours), changelog (hours), marketing (at launch), press (after).

### Slot 03 · not built

Empty. The shelf is built to hold a dozen. Nothing is planned publicly, and there
is no roadmap to quote. Tool requests are welcome at request@gledach.de, and
requests that would help more people than the person asking are prioritised.

## Previews

Convention: `<tool>.gledach.de`. One per tool, replaced in place. A preview is a
static export of a real deployment: real data, dated, read only. A re-export
overwrites it, so a preview is the most recent snapshot rather than an archive.
